reference.source: KD Tripathi Essentials of Medical Pharmacology 8th Edition and Kaplan Pharmacology (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Intramuscular adrenaline is the only life saving drug in anaphylaxis
Noradrenaline is first line vasopressor in septic shock
Phenylephrine raises pressure with reflex bradycardia
Salbutamol shifts potassium into cells in hyperkalaemia
reference.pathophysiology: Catecholamines act through G protein coupled receptors raising cyclic AMP in heart and bronchi (beta) or calcium mediated vasoconstriction (alpha 1), and are cleared by neuronal reuptake plus MAO and COMT metabolism. Shock states differ in whether vessels, pump or both have failed, so receptor targeted selection restores perfusion without excess myocardial oxygen cost.
additionalDifferentials: Adrenaline versus noradrenaline versus phenylephrine profiles
Direct versus indirect sympathomimetics and tachyphylaxis
additionalInvestigations: Lactate and perfusion guided shock resuscitation
Echocardiography to separate pump from vessel failure
